task.title: Prepare a bank reconciliation for October
task.brief: Take about 20 minutes. Using the figures below, write: (1) the entries that must go in the cash book, with the adjusted cash book balance; (2) a simple bank reconciliation statement that shows the bank balance and the adjusted cash book balance agree; and (3) one line on what you would follow up. Show your working in plain steps. A good answer gets the right balance, puts each item on the correct side, and is easy to check.
task.material:
Business: Sai Krishna Traders. Month: October.
Cash book (bank column) balance on 31 Oct: ₹80,000 (debit)
Bank statement balance on 31 Oct: ₹91,200 (credit)
Found while checking:
1. Cheque no. 2241 given to Lakshmi Traders for ₹12,000 on 29 Oct is not yet cashed.
2. Cheque for ₹6,000 from Rao & Sons, deposited on 31 Oct, is not yet credited by the bank.
3. Bank charges of ₹350 are on the statement but not in the cash book.
4. Interest of ₹450 credited by the bank is not in the cash book.
5. Meera Stores paid ₹5,100 by NEFT straight into the bank. Not in the cash book.
key_points: Cash book entries: less bank charges ₹350, add interest ₹450, add NEFT from Meera Stores ₹5,100
Bank side: ₹91,200 less unpresented cheque ₹12,000 plus uncleared deposit ₹6,000 = ₹85,200
Meera Stores' account is credited with ₹5,100
Follow up the uncleared Rao & Sons cheque and the unpresented Lakshmi Traders cheque

rubric.label: Correct figures
rubric.guide: 0 = wrong balance and sides, 3 = some items right but the balances don't agree, 5 = all items on the right side and both balances are ₹85,200

rubric.label: Completeness
rubric.guide: 0 = only a final number, 3 = statement or entries missing, 5 = entries, adjusted balance, statement and follow-up all given

rubric.label: Clear working
rubric.guide: 0 = can't follow, 3 = working shown but untidy, 5 = neat steps a senior can check quickly
